messages.author: 4ead13a5eaad2fc6
messages.subject: Caching using children documents?
parts:
I'm working on a relatively large document using knitr for the first
time. The way i had envisioned working was having one master tex or
rnw file that contained inputs (either include, or using knitr's
knit_child function) to the chapters I'm writing. I've run into a
series of problems that are almost certainly my unfamiliarity with
knitr and best practices for this kind of setup.

First, when I use the knit_child documents and just run knit on the
parent document (with caching) I will frequently get errors like the
following the second or third time I run knit.

Quitting from lines 103-NA: Error in exists(str_c(".", hash), envir =
globalenv(), mode = "character") :
internal error -3 in R_decompress1

These errors go away if I erase the cache, but come back if I run it
again. I haven't had much time to investigate where exactly it's
breaking down (deadlines, sorry!), but that's the error I'm getting
when it breaks.

I've finally got a system that seems to be working where I knit the
child documents separately, then compile the main tex document on it's
own (using the package import to allow for figures, etc. to be in
subdirectories of the path of the main document). This works, although
is far from ideal. Does anyone have any suggestions on a better
workflow, or what I'm messing up to get these cache issues? Thanks.

messages.author: 881c51ed14655bd5
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Caching using children documents?
parts:
For large projects I find that individual processing of files
optionally with a makefile is the best approach. The error that you
are getting is when you have undetected environment manipulations that
are not cached, something like a setup block that loads the libraries
should never be cached. Probably something along those lines is what
is happening here. Unless there is a specific reason for a child
document It is better to process the documents separately. I even go
as far as explicitly caching the results with RData files to make sure
that I can pick up anywhere I need to.

-Andrew

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Caching using children documents?
parts:
That is often an indication that the cache was corrupted for some
reason. What is your sessionInfo()?

I guess I also saw that error message long time ago, but have not seen
it recently. If I were to give any advice, I would recommend you to
always knit the document in a clean non-interactive R session, e.g.
call knitr through Rscript rather than starting an interactive R
session and library(knitr); knit(...).

Regards,
Yihui
